title: fix(shapes): bitmap fill type bytes 0x40/0x42 are swapped (smooth vs non-smooth inverted)
description:
## Bug

Both packages/swf/src/shapes.ts and packages/swf/src/morphshape.ts use an inverted mapping for bitmap fill type bytes. The smooth vs non-smooth variants are swapped.

## Root cause

Both files contain:

  if (fill.repeat && fill.smooth) fillTypeByte = 0x42;       // WRONG: should be 0x40
  else if (fill.repeat && !fill.smooth) fillTypeByte = 0x40; // WRONG: should be 0x42
  else if (!fill.repeat && fill.smooth) fillTypeByte = 0x43; // WRONG: should be 0x41
  else fillTypeByte = 0x41;                                  // WRONG: should be 0x43

## Correct mapping (per ruffle swf/src/write.rs lines 1569-1573)

  (smoothed=true,  repeating=true)  -> 0x40
  (smoothed=true,  repeating=false) -> 0x41
  (smoothed=false, repeating=true)  -> 0x42
  (smoothed=false, repeating=false) -> 0x43

Confirmed by ruffle write.rs (lines 1569-1573) and unit tests (read.rs lines 2962-2983).

The bug exists in both shapes.ts (lines 546-549) and morphshape.ts writeMorphFillStyleArray (lines 430-433).

## Effect

Any bitmap fill with smooth=true is emitted with the non-smoothed type byte and vice-versa. Ruffle renders bitmap fills with incorrect smoothing. The wrong comments in both files caused the incorrect implementation.

## Fix

In both shapes.ts and morphshape.ts, correct the mapping to:

  if (fill.repeat && fill.smooth) fillTypeByte = 0x40;
  else if (fill.repeat && !fill.smooth) fillTypeByte = 0x42;
  else if (!fill.repeat && fill.smooth) fillTypeByte = 0x41;
  else fillTypeByte = 0x43;

And update the comments to match ruffle's write.rs semantics.
